Every section of the workshop has a notebook. Additional notebooks offer
deep dives: four are opened live and finished at home, four are take-home
from the start. They are **English-primary**, and every heading
carries a one-line Spanish summary — *cada encabezado lleva un resumen en
español.*

## How they are built

<span data-language-key="how-they-are-built"></span>

Notebooks 01–11 separate the live session from later study:

1. **Header:** **Practise today** and **Explore later**, with the same outcomes as the slides and handbook.
2. **Run the Setup cell first, then work straight down.** Each notebook opens
   with a short route to follow: a quick recall, a worked example, then your
   own attempt, feedback, and a checkpoint. Try the exercise yourself before
   opening the folded solution.
3. **Core complete:** the route above ends here. Keep your explanation —
   that is what the session needs — and follow the facilitator's quiz and
   break schedule.
4. **Explore later:** optional material you come back to afterward — more
   reference, exercises, and explorers.

Notebook 00 keeps the entry check and pre-work setup; 12 starts with the exit check. The deep dives are listed under **Going further** below. Solutions remain folded: open them after an attempt. Each notebook loads its own data and runs independently.

::: {.callout-important appearance="simple"}
The notebooks are committed with **no outputs and no execution counts**. Every
number you see is one you produced. The prose quotes the expected results, so
you can tell whether yours are right. If yours differ, that is worth
investigating rather than dismissing.
:::

## Going further

<span data-language-key="going-further"></span>

These are **not sections**. They are deep dives, and they have no slides and
no Kahoot. Four are opened live, as a 20- or 25-minute lab each: **17**
(attention) before lunch, then **13** (convolution), **14** (CP) and **20**
(AlphaTensor) in the afternoon. The room works the notebook's core route and
takes the rest home. The other four — 15, 16, 18 and 19 — are take-home
material with no minutes on the workshop clock. Section 11's live core compares CP and Tucker using library calls; its
four-model overview is extension material. Notebooks 14 and 15 build on that
comparison by fitting CP by hand and then changing what "fit" means.

{{< include _includes/notebooks-extra-en.md >}}

Deep dive 19 works through the ML blog post *CP or Tucker in practice*.

Deep dive 20 works through the three *AlphaTensor* posts on the ML blog: it
writes matrix multiplication as a tensor, plays the search for a faster
algorithm as a game on the smallest case, and checks the factorisations
DeepMind published. It trains nothing.

The browser widgets beside the sections have a page of their own:
[Interactive](interactive.qmd) gives each one a card, with the sections it
belongs to and the scenes worth opening directly.

## Running them somewhere other than Colab

<span data-language-key="running-them-somewhere-other-than-colab"></span>

The notebooks only need the scientific Python stack. Locally:

```bash
git clone {{< var repo.url >}}.git
cd {{< var repo.name >}}
uv run --group notebooks jupyter lab
```

The `notebooks` group is declared in `pyproject.toml`, and it is read off the
notebooks' own imports rather than written down beside them. `matplotlib` and
`ipywidgets` are in it because the notebooks use plots and interactive widgets.
Both ship with Colab, so a missing one only shows up when you run locally.

`scikit-learn` and `scikit-image` ship the tumour data, the handwritten digits
and the photographs. Some notebooks use only bundled data; others download
data or install packages. The generated table below lists each notebook's
network requirements.
